solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Glue rifle butt, not taking seconds. That's sound for some time

indicators.note: not taking means the letters named next are left out of both words before them

parts.note: to stick is to glue
the stock is the butt end of a rifle
S is the abbreviation for second, so seconds supplies two of them, one from each word

explanation.surface: A gunsmith repairs a rifle butt in a hurry, with a clock ticking in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not taking' removes an S from each of STICK and STOCK, leaving TICK and TOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The paired syllables imitate the beat of a clock, the noise heard while time passes.

clue.text: Spring up from vagrant, old and rank

parts.note: a tramp is a vagrant
a line or rank is a row of people

explanation.surface: A down-and-out who is old and smelly leaps to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like an adjective meaning smelly, but it is a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast bounces up off this sprung canvas, so it is something to leap up from.

clue.text: Company gets on top of new scam

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A firm gets to the bottom of a newly-launched fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A con trick is a swindle or confidence fraud.

clue.text: Where there's a will, there's a —

definitions.text: Where there's a will, there's a —

parts.words: Where there's a will, there's a —
parts.note: the proverb ends 'way', but taken literally, someone who leaves a will is in a particular legal condition

explanation.surface: The old proverb about determination finding a path, left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having made a legally valid will is said to die in this condition.

clue.text: Artful Charlie going to bar more than once

indicators.note: more than once means the joined pieces are repeated

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a lever is a bar used to prise things

explanation.surface: A crafty fellow called Charlie keeps going to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' tempts as a pub, but it is a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: Showily or excessively ingenious describes someone too crafty for their own good.

clue.text: Composer writing feature about opus

indicators.note: about means the facial word goes round the abbreviation for the work

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a numbered musical work

explanation.surface: A music journalist is writing a feature article about one particular opus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' suggests a newspaper article, but it is a feature of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the Polish Romantic composer of piano nocturnes and études.

clue.text: Regular visitor put somewhat in shade

indicators.note: put signals placing one piece in another
in shows the phrase for somewhat goes inside the word for shade

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a bit means somewhat

explanation.surface: A frequent guest is put somewhat in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitué is someone who frequents a place, like a café or club, as a regular.

clue.text: Prayer gives one lift

definitions.meaning: a type of elevator with open cars moving continuously in a loop

explanation.surface: Saying prayers raises one's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin 'Our Father' is the prayer; the endless-loop elevator is named from its rosary-like chain.

clue.text: Where conductors meet to agree on technique, ultimately

parts.note: to nod is to agree

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of technique

explanation.surface: Orchestra conductors meet to agree on a technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductors' suggests orchestra leaders; they are electrical conductors joining at a junction.
explanation.definitionFit: In a circuit a node is a junction point where wires or components connect.

clue.text: Badly sung idea for a religious piece

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A choir performs a poorly sung piece of music, with a vague idea of a better one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lamb of God section of the Mass is often set to music as a sacred choral piece.

clue.text: Died down and burned away, last of coal not needed

indicators.note: not needed means that letter is dropped from the word for burned away

parts.note: ablated means worn or burned away, as a spacecraft heat shield is

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word coal

explanation.surface: A coal fire died down and burned away until no more coal was needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm or fever that has abated has lessened or subsided in intensity.

clue.text: This fixes pitches, yet using rake is wrong

indicators.note: is wrong means the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A groundsman is told that using a rake to repair sports pitches is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitches' suggests sports grounds, but they are musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharps or flats at the start of a stave set which notes are played raised or lowered.

clue.text: Soldiers beheaded Achilles' foe — not state business

parts.note: privates are ordinary soldiers of the lowest rank

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off the Trojan hero's name

parts.note: Hector, the Trojan prince, was killed by Achilles in the Iliad

explanation.surface: Soldiers have beheaded the enemy of Achilles, a grisly matter that is no business of the state.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of an economy run by private companies stands in contrast to state-owned enterprise.

clue.text: Bury coins where roads meet

parts.note: to inter is to bury
change is loose coins

explanation.surface: Someone hides a hoard of money at a crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorway junction with slip roads and bridges is a grade-separated junction of this kind.

clue.text: What draws little money to protect unwell these days

indicators.note: to protect means the money word surrounds the word for unwell

parts.note: pence are small coins, little amounts of money
ill means unwell
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A small sum is set aside to look after a sick person nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws' suggests attracting, but it means drawing pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The graphite core of a pencil is the part that makes marks on paper.

clue.text: In a spot, perhaps, the man is flexible

parts.note: anything in a spotlight is lit; the perhaps marks a spotlight as one example of lighting
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man caught in a tight spot proves to be agile enough to wriggle out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a spot' reads as 'in trouble', but here it means standing in a spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithe body is supple and bends easily, like a gymnast's or a dancer's.

clue.text: Dish inducting fool into Creole cooking

indicators.note: inducting means bringing someone in, so the fool is enrolled within the other letters
into marks where the fool goes: inside the rearranged Creole letters
cooking means the letters of Creole are stirred into a new order

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A chef adds something foolish to a dish while doing Creole cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like part of the cooking scene, but it alone is the definition; 'cooking' is the anagram signal and 'inducting ... into' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a slow-cooked stew baked in a covered pot, a classic one-pot dish.

clue.text: German town burger men upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some men in Germany are annoyed about their burgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burger' hints at Hamburg, a decoy German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuremberg is a city in Bavaria, famous for its medieval old town and postwar trials.

clue.text: Damage most of camping man's tent

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: queen is slang for a camp, effeminate man

explanation.surface: Someone damages the tent of a man on a camping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camping' suggests a camping trip, but it means camp in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A large canvas tent used for weddings or fêtes is called a marquee.

clue.text: Eye work that gets a lot of credit

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a job that pays well enough to earn plenty of credit.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK is British slang for credit, as in buying something on tick.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is a dated or jocular word for an eye, from the Greek for sight.

clue.text: City tree has to come down

parts.note: the oak is a tree
to land is to come down to earth

explanation.surface: A tree in town has to be felled.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakland is a port city in California, across the bay from San Francisco.

clue.text: Rocks here seething with male fish

indicators.note: seething means churning violently, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Waves churn around rocks where male fish gather.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad, a bony relative of jacks found in the Atlantic, is a type of sea fish.

clue.text: Team's cancelling southern date in Rome

indicators.note: cancelling means that letter is struck out

parts.note: side is a team, and the 's is read as is, giving sides

explanation.surface: A football team calls off a trip south to Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides fell mid-month, the 15th of March being the famous one.

clue.text: True Australian is mostly stupid about tattoo

indicators.note: about means the shortened word for stupid goes round the tattoo word
mostly means all but the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: dumb means stupid
ink is slang for a tattoo

explanation.surface: An Aussie, rather dim, has had a tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the word for stupid, and 'about' wraps it round the tattoo; 'fair dinkum' is the familiar Australian phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinkum, as in fair dinkum, is Australian slang for genuine or honest.

clue.text: People in country to appeal about invading Vikings

indicators.note: about means the word for appeal wraps around the Vikings

parts.note: to sue is to appeal or plead, as in suing for peace
the Danes were the Vikings who invaded England

explanation.surface: A nation's people plead for help against Viking invaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Those from Sudan, the African nation, are its nationals or citizens.

clue.text: I pass after end of course

indicators.note: after puts the word for pass behind that letter
end of points to the last letter of course

parts.note: to go is to pass, as in time going by

explanation.surface: A student passes once the course has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for the first-person pronoun and names the self in psychology.

clue.text: Sound is harsh, missing out on gold disc

indicators.note: missing out on means the chemical symbol for gold is dropped

parts.note: austere means severe or harsh
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
O is a disc shape

explanation.surface: An athlete harshly misses out on a gold medal, that disc of glory.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-channel audio reproduction is commonly used as a noun for a hi-fi or its sound.

clue.text: Where film stage went for useless employees

definitions.meaning: the ... stagecoach is sung of in the film Calamity Jane, heading to that South Dakota town
staff no longer productive and fit to be cut

explanation.surface: A film studio's soundstage was moved to make room for workers who do nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' is a stagecoach, not a film set: Doris Day sings of the Deadwood Stage in Calamity Jane.
explanation.definitionFit: Unproductive staff are likened to dead branches on a tree that need pruning.
